tell: A CDK4/6 inhibitor largely recovered in feces, about 81% of a dose, and dosed twice daily.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is 45% after a single 200 mg oral dose, and a high-fat meal changes exposure only slightly. Bound to plasma proteins at 96.3%, it is cleared mainly by hepatic metabolism.
The active moiety has a molecular weight of 506.59 and is a white to yellow powder.
Approved under an NDA as tablets of 50, 100, 150 and 200 mg, taken twice daily.
No boxed warning and no contraindications. Diarrhea and infections are among the most common adverse reactions.
Adjuvant treatment of early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence, and advanced breast cancer, in hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative disease.
Inhibits cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6, which blocks retinoblastoma protein phosphorylation and halts cell-cycle progression from G1 into S phase.
The generic name begins with A and has eleven letters.
